summary.headline: Arihant Superstructures' H1 FY27 bookings fell to INR 345.8 crore (about 27% lower YoY in Q2 as units sold dropped from 280 to 236), with management guiding 20% revenue growth and 25%+ EBITDA margin.
summary.overview: Management reported H1 FY27 operating revenue of INR 265 crore (about 9% YoY), EBITDA of INR 56 crore at a 20.97% margin, and PAT of INR 20.3 crore. Q2 consolidated revenue was INR 133 crore (about 9% YoY), EBITDA INR 28 crore (down 7% YoY), and PAT INR 10.6 crore. Q2 bookings were 236 units / 2.2 lakh sq ft / INR 173 crore, with management attributing the softer sales to a focus on existing multi-phase inventory and launches pushed to Q3-Q4 in Panvel. Management also outlined hospitality and annuity projects at Chowk (ITC Hotels 227-room hotel, Club 10 Gymkhana, 108-key budget hotel) and reiterated a 20% FY27 revenue growth target.

segments.name: Residential sales (Q2 FY27)
segments.commentary: 236 units, 2.2 lakh sq ft, INR 173 crore booking value; average price INR 7,822/sq ft vs INR 7,500 in Q1 FY27; average ticket INR 73.15 lakh. Collections INR 154.5 crore.

segments.name: Residential sales (H1 FY27)
segments.commentary: 457 units, 4.52 lakh sq ft, INR 345.8 crore; average INR 7,650/sq ft vs INR 7,500 in H1 FY26; average ticket INR 75.6 lakh. Collections INR 316 crore. Unsold ready inventory about 275 units worth INR 53 crore.

segments.name: Hospitality (World Villas, Chowk)
segments.commentary: Agreement signed 24 Sep with ITC Hotels for a 227-room luxury hotel (44 suites, Mementos by ITC) on a 10-acre parcel; management contract model, construction about 3 years, revenue from FY29.

segments.name: Club 10 Gymkhana / budget hotel
segments.commentary: First slab cast; more than 800 memberships gathered. A 108-key budget hotel announced, operator talks ongoing.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at about 20% YoY, supported by OCs expected by year-end for 1 Tower at Arihant Aspire and Arihant Advika in Vashi.
EBITDA margin to be targeted at upwards of 25% on a full-year basis; quarterly margins can vary with project mix.
Average cost of debt about 13% today, expected to fall to about 12.5% by end of FY27; STCI loan refinanced with ICICI Bank, cost cut from 11.75% to 8.6%.
Q3 and Q4 launches lined up in Panvel to lift presales; festive-season quarters historically stronger.
Town Villas launch pushed to FY28; society redevelopment DA expected to be signed by Q3.
Annuity income from hotel and Club 10 Gymkhana expected from FY30 (earlier comment on hotel revenue from FY29).
capex_capacity: World Villas Phase 1 (about 178 villas) launched; about 60 sold to date; balance sales expected over the next 2 years. Total GDV about INR 1,200 crore for 391 villas.
Town Villas at Chowk: land increased to about 99.5 acres (from about 76 acres a year ago); saleable area about 58 lakh sq ft, GDV about INR 4,800 crore; approvals still in progress.
Shilphata JV: 14% area to landowner, 86% to company.
Jodhpur: sell-and-build model, building-by-building development; clubhouse completed at Arihant Anchal.
Total land under work about 320 acres; unstarted land about 99.5 acres at Chowk and 7-8 acres at Panvel.
Hotel and Gymkhana financing to come mainly from external debt, as they have no pre-sales.
demand_pricing: Management said demand has held steady over the last year and prices are rising across major markets; buyers are moving up the price ladder.

Affordability and down payments are a constraint for the affordable segment; mid-income (INR 50 lakh to 1.5 crore) is absorbing well at Kharghar, Panvel and Shilphata; luxury is performing better than the other two segments.
Raw material and labour costs stayed tight; total construction cost up 4-5% over the last 8-9 months, with management saying all escalations are built in and that it prefers pricing over volume.
Management expects interest rates to rise a further 25-50 bps in coming quarters.
Data centres ruled out for now due to inadequate power and water infrastructure at Panvel outskirts; hospitality is the preferred alternative use.

qa_highlights.question: Rising interest rates: what is the demand outlook for affordable and mid-income housing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said demand is good but affordability and own contribution are the constraints; walk-ins and enquiries are rising, and mid-income is absorbing well.

qa_highlights.question: Why did presales fall about 27% YoY in Q2, with units down from 280 to 236?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the focus was on existing inventory in multi-phase projects; more launches are planned in Panvel for Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the raw material and gross margin decline is commodity inflation versus project mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the P&L margin movement to project mix and said raw material costs rose about 4-5% of total construction cost over 8-9 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the blended cost of debt and finance cost trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Average cost of debt about 13%, expected to fall to about 12.5% by year-end; gross debt about INR 900 crore, with Q2 interest of INR 14.8 crore, down 13% YoY.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 revenue guidance and which projects drive H2 recognition?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is 20% revenue growth for FY27, driven by OCs at Arihant Aspire and Arihant Advika (Vashi) by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin should be modelled for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said to target EBITDA margin upwards of 25% on a full-year basis.

qa_highlights.question: Is operating cash flow sustainable, and when will cash flow be positive after hotel and Gymkhana capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the hotel and Gymkhana sit in separate entities or use different revenue recognition and will be debt-financed; the other projects are cash-positive from operations.

qa_highlights.question: When will annuity income from the hotel and Gymkhana contribute?

risks_watch: Q2 presales down about 27% YoY; Q3-Q4 Panvel launches must convert to lift bookings.
Gross margin decline (raw material inflation and project mix); quarterly EBITDA margin at about 21% versus 25%+ annual target.
Net debt of INR 827 crore and INR 435 crore of unsecured loans; hotel and Gymkhana to be funded by external debt with no pre-sales.
Rising interest-rate environment, with a further 25-50 bps increase flagged by management.
Approval timelines for Town Villas (launch pushed to FY28) and society redevelopment DA (targeted by Q3).
Hotel operator for the 108-key budget hotel not yet finalised.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, pricing and margin targets, but cautious on near-term sales volumes and affordability. Management deflected on a few specifics (society redevelopment terms, Town Villas approvals, data centre plans) and stated that several items are still in progress.
key_quotes: Our approach is to recover these increases through pricing on unsold inventory rather than chase volume at the cost of margin.
We should be targeting EBITDA margins upwards of 25% on a total financial year basis.
We have built in all the escalations.
Average cost of debt today will be around 13%, and we expect that to drop down to around 12.5% by end of this financial year.

growth.why: Management reiterated about 20% FY27 revenue growth, but H1 revenue grew only about 9% and Q2 bookings fell to INR 173 crore (236 units vs 280), so backing is partial: OCs for Arihant Aspire and Advika expected by year-end, Panvel launches in Q3-Q4, and rising realisations (INR 7,822/sq ft in Q2), with the hotel and Town Villas not contributing until FY28-FY29.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management is targeting EBITDA margin upwards of 25% for full FY27, versus H1 at 20.97% and Q2 at about 21%, so H2 must run well above 25% to hit the target; the gap is a credibility risk.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: ITC-branded 227-room hotel is under construction for about 3 years with revenue from FY29, and OCs for Arihant Aspire and Advika in Vashi are expected by year-end, though Town Villas launch is pushed to FY28 and the 108-key hotel has no operator yet.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 bookings were 457 units and INR 345.8 crore, with Q2 units down from 280 to 236 (about -16%) and bookings down about 27% YoY; Panvel launches in Q3-Q4 must convert to lift volumes.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is not disclosed, but the 108-key budget hotel is announced and the society redevelopment DA is targeted by Q3 on about 99.5 acres of unstarted land at Chowk, so new commitments are plausible; hotel and Gymkhana will be debt-funded with no pre-sales.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: H1 revenue grew only about 9% YoY against a 20% FY27 guide, so reaching the target needs an H2 surge from OCs and Panvel launches; an upgrade is not supported by the numbers.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 revenue growth of about 9% versus 20% guided, Q2 presales down about 27% YoY and quarterly EBITDA margin about 21% versus the 25%+ target all leave the FY27 guidance at risk, though management reiterated it.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management has lined up Panvel launches for Q3 and Q4 to lift presales, with the festive quarters historically stronger; Town Villas is pushed to FY28 and the 108-key budget hotel is only at operator-talk stage.

rows.label: Realisation rising and pricing preferred over volume
rows.why: Average price rose to INR 7,822/sq ft in Q2 from INR 7,500 in Q1 (about +4%), and management said construction costs are up 4-5% with all escalations built in and it prefers pricing over volume.

rows.label: STCI loan refinanced to ICICI Bank at 8.6%
rows.why: Refinancing cut the cost from 11.75% to 8.6% and average cost of debt is guided to fall from about 13% to 12.5% by FY27 end, though net debt is INR 827 crore and rates may rise 25-50 bps.

rows.label: ITC Hotels luxury hotel agreement signed
rows.why: Agreement was signed 24 Sep for a 227-room hotel on a 10-acre parcel under a management contract; revenue starts FY29 and annuity income from FY30, so it adds no FY27 earnings.

tone.note: Management was confident on pricing, the 20% FY27 revenue target, the 25%+ margin goal and the cost of debt falling, but cautious on Q2 sales volumes and affordability; analysts pressed on the presales drop, margin mix and cash burn from hotel and Gymkhana, and management deflected on society redeve
